where it is used substantively for λιτάς [suppliant]. In M ἀμφίλιταν [around the suppliant] from the first hand, ἀμφὶ λιτάν [around the suppliant] from a recent hand. Seidler correctly read ἀμφὶ λίταν [around the suppliant], except that, as Hermann pointed out, he should have written λιτάν᾽ [suppliant]. For similar adjectives ending in -ανος are oxytone according to the rule of Herodian in Arcadius p. 64, 21.
Here too I corrected the accent, which in M is λίτανα [suppliant].
